title: Unify the game UI and establish reusable templates
outcome: From opening the game to managing a colony and saving or loading it, players use one readable gothic industrial interface with predictable controls and state feedback.
scope: Shared Unity uGUI theme tokens, type hierarchy, spacing, semantic colors, and accessible control states
Reusable UI components and layouts for screens, HUD bars, panels, dialogs, tooltips, toasts, and the future vox portrait card

All player-facing surfaces: title, setup, landing, HUD, build and placement, inspectors and ship, industry, resources and surveys, research, guide, mining, earthworks, urban development, events, and save/load feedback
Inventory and migration of existing local-only cinematic and urban screens after their source is available in an agreed branch
nonGoals: Change gameplay rules, bindings, camera behavior, save data, or Unity rendering pipeline
Replace the cinematic world backdrop or copy official game UI assets
Redesign editor and developer diagnostics as player UI
acceptance: A title → new game → landing → build → inspect → save → load playthrough keeps all existing actions, values and states
All in-scope screens use the documented theme and shared components, including enabled, focused, disabled, warning and critical states
Representative screens are visually reviewed at 1280×800, 1920×1080, and ultrawide; long labels and dense panels remain readable and interactive
A small documented template example and guard check catch new hardcoded shared style values and ad hoc controls outside agreed exceptions
A portrait-card template can display a character, speaker role, priority, message and optional relevant action without stealing game input
rollback: Split template and screen migration into reviewable pull requests. Revert a migration slice while its legacy UI remains available. Preserve scene and asset GUIDs.

design.reference: Issue #24 design review: keep existing uGUI and screen wiring, centralize visual construction, preserve modal/input semantics, and handle in-progress menu/urban integration separately.

designApproval.reference: Codex chat, 2026-11-07: “approve both designs” after review of issues #24 and #25.
